newsitem.title: USA: Detroit Purchasing Mgrs October index falls.
newsitem.headline: Detroit Purchasing Mgrs October index falls.

text.p: The Detroit Purchasing Managers' composite index fell slightly to 59.7 in October from 59.9 in September, according to a Comerica Inc survey released Thursday.
An index below 50 signals a slowing manufacturing economy, while a reading above 50 suggests expansion.
The prices paid index was 52.9 in October versus 50.0 in September. The employment component of the barometer was 55.5 in October versus 58.5 in September.

"October's survey reveals a very solid growth situation for Southeastern Michigan, with new orders and production leading the way," said David Littmann, senior economist with Detroit-based Comerica Bank.

"The expansion continues to be balanced, but the automotive sector is once again more robust than the other sectors. This is highlighted in the price and shortages portions of our survey," Littmann noted.

Comerica's composite index is based on surveys of local purchasing managers belonging to the 500-member National Association of Purchasing Management-Metro Detroit.
